question: What does section 4 of the Income Tax Ordinance impose tax on, and at which rates?
reference_answer: Income tax is imposed for each tax year on every person who has taxable income for the year, at the rates in Division I or II of Part I of the First Schedule; tax credits are then subtracted from the resulting amount.

question: At what rate is the surcharge under section 4AB charged, and above what level of taxable income?
reference_answer: Individuals and associations of persons pay a surcharge of ten percent of the income tax under Division I of Part I of the First Schedule where taxable income exceeds Rs. 10 million.

question: Does a salaried individual earning more than Rs. 10 million have to pay the section 4AB surcharge?
reference_answer: No. The proviso to section 4AB says no surcharge is payable by an individual deriving income chargeable under the head 'Salary'.

question: From which tax year is super tax on high earning persons imposed under section 4C?
reference_answer: Super tax under section 4C is imposed for tax year 2022 and onwards at the rates in Division IIB of Part I of the First Schedule.

question: What is the super tax rate for a banking company whose income exceeds Rs. 150 million?
reference_answer: 10% of the income (Division IIB, Part I, First Schedule, serial 1), levied under section 4C.

question: What super tax rate applies to a person other than a bank, a fertilizer seller or a Fifth Schedule person whose income exceeds Rs. 500 million?
reference_answer: 8% of the income (Division IIB, Part I, First Schedule, serial 4).

question: How is tax on dividends computed under section 5?
reference_answer: By applying the rate in Division III of Part I of the First Schedule to the gross amount of the dividend; the section does not apply to exempt dividends.

question: Does the separate tax on profit on debt under section 7B apply if my profit on debt exceeds Rs. 5 million?
reference_answer: No. Section 7B does not apply to profit on debt that is exempt or that exceeds five million rupees.

question: How is taxable income defined in the Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: Taxable income is the person's total income for the tax year reduced (but not below zero) by the total deductible allowances under Part IX of Chapter III.

question: What are the heads of income under the Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: Salary; Income from Property; Income from Business; Capital Gains; and Income from Other Sources.

question: Are overtime payments and bonuses part of salary for income tax purposes?
reference_answer: Yes. Salary includes pay, wages and other remuneration such as leave pay, overtime, bonus, commission, fees, gratuity and work-condition supplements.

question: Is a fixed monthly travel or rent allowance paid by my employer included in my salary?
reference_answer: Yes. Allowances such as cost of living, rent, utilities, education, entertainment or travel are salary; only allowances solely expended in performing duties are excluded, and a fixed monthly allowance or one not wholly spent on behalf of the employer does not count as solely expended.

question: How is a car provided by an employer for an employee's private use taxed?
reference_answer: The employee's salary for the year includes an amount computed as prescribed for the private use of the motor vehicle.

question: What counts as 'rent' under section 15 of the Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: Any amount received or receivable by the owner of land or a building for the use or occupation (or right to use or occupy) of it, including a forfeited deposit under a contract for sale of land or a building.

question: Is agricultural income taxable under the federal Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: No. Agricultural income, such as rent or revenue from land in Pakistan used for agricultural purposes, is exempt under section 41.

question: Is a scholarship received to pay for my education taxable?
reference_answer: No, a scholarship granted to meet the cost of education is exempt, unless it is paid directly or indirectly by an associate.

question: Is support money received by a spouse under an agreement to live apart taxable?
reference_answer: No. Income received by a spouse as support payment under an agreement to live apart is exempt.

question: For how long is the foreign-source income of a returning Pakistani expatriate exempt?
reference_answer: It is exempt in the tax year the citizen becomes a resident and in the following tax year, provided the person was not resident in any of the four preceding tax years.

question: When is the foreign-source income of a short-term resident individual exempt?
reference_answer: When the individual is resident solely because of employment and is present in Pakistan for no more than three years; it does not apply to income from a business established in Pakistan or to foreign-source income brought into or received in Pakistan.

question: For how many years can an unabsorbed business loss be carried forward?
reference_answer: A business loss not set off can be carried forward against business income, but not to more than six tax years immediately succeeding the year in which the loss was first computed.

question: Can I set off a capital loss against my salary income?
reference_answer: No. A capital loss cannot be set off against income under any other head; it is carried forward and set off only against capital gains of later years.

question: Can I claim Zakat paid as a deduction, and can unused Zakat be carried forward?
reference_answer: Zakat paid under the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980 is a deductible allowance; any part that cannot be deducted in the year is not refunded or carried forward or back.

question: Who can claim the deductible allowance for children's tuition fee, and how much?
reference_answer: An individual with taxable income below Rs. 1.5 million; the allowance is the lesser of 5% of tuition fee paid, 25% of taxable income, and Rs. 60,000 multiplied by the number of children.

question: Is Workers' Welfare Fund paid by a business deductible?
reference_answer: Yes. Workers' Welfare Fund paid under the 1971 Ordinance or a provincial WWF law is a deductible allowance (not for amounts paid to Provinces by a trans-provincial establishment).

question: Do I get a tax benefit for donating to a public university?
reference_answer: Yes. Donations to a board of education or a university established under Federal or Provincial law qualify for a tax credit under section 61, computed by formula.

question: Who is entitled to a tax credit for contributions to an approved pension fund?
reference_answer: An eligible person (section 2(19A)) with salary or business income who contributes to an approved pension fund under the Voluntary Pension System Rules, 2005.

question: Is there a tax credit for profit paid on a housing loan?
reference_answer: Yes. An individual gets a tax credit for profit on debt paid on a loan from a scheduled bank or other specified lender used to construct or acquire one personal house within the section's limits.

question: What is the 'tax year' under the Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: A twelve-month period ending on 30 June (the normal tax year), named after the calendar year in which that date falls.

question: How many days must an individual be present in Pakistan to be a resident individual?
reference_answer: 183 days or more in the tax year (in one or more periods).

question: Can a Pakistani citizen who spends much of the year abroad still be a resident individual?
reference_answer: Yes, if the citizen is not present in any other country for more than 182 days in the tax year, or is not a resident taxpayer of any other country.

question: When is a company treated as a resident company?
reference_answer: If it is incorporated under Pakistani law, its control and management is wholly in Pakistan at any time in the year, or it is a Provincial Government or Local Government.

question: Is foreign salary received by a resident individual taxed in Pakistan if tax was already paid abroad?
reference_answer: It is exempt if foreign income tax was paid on it, e.g. withheld by the employer and paid to the foreign country's revenue authority.

question: How much foreign tax credit is allowed on foreign-source income?
reference_answer: The lesser of the foreign income tax paid and the Pakistan tax payable on that income.

question: When is salary Pakistan-source income?
reference_answer: When it is from employment exercised in Pakistan (wherever paid), or when it is paid by the Federal, a Provincial or a Local Government wherever the employment is exercised.

question: What happens if I cannot explain the source of an investment or money I own?
reference_answer: If no explanation is offered, or the Commissioner finds it unsatisfactory, the unexplained amount is included in the person's income chargeable to tax.

question: Which persons are covered by minimum tax under section 113?
reference_answer: Resident companies, permanent establishments of non-resident companies, and individuals and AOPs with turnover of Rs. 100 million or more in tax year 2017 or later.

question: Who is required to file an income tax return?
reference_answer: Among others: every company; every other person whose taxable income exceeds the non-taxable limit; non-profit organizations; persons whose income is subject to final taxation; and persons meeting the conditions in section 114(1)(b).

question: If I own a house on a plot of 500 square yards, do I have to file a tax return even with no taxable income?
reference_answer: Yes. Section 114(1)(b) requires a return from a person who owns immovable property with land area of 500 square yards or more in the specified areas.

question: Does a widow who owns a 500 square yard house have to file a return only because of that property?
reference_answer: No. Section 115(3) exempts a widow, an orphan under 25, a disabled person, and (for property) a non-resident from filing solely because of those property clauses of section 114.

question: Who has to file a foreign income and assets statement?
reference_answer: A resident individual with foreign income of at least USD 10,000 or foreign assets worth at least USD 100,000.

question: What can the Commissioner ask for in a wealth statement?
reference_answer: By notice, an individual's total assets and liabilities (including foreign ones) and those of the spouse, minor children and other dependents, as of the dates specified.

question: What is the due date for a salaried individual to file the income tax return?
reference_answer: On or before 30 September following the end of the tax year.

question: By when must a company whose tax year ends between 1 January and 30 June file its return?
reference_answer: On or before 31 December following the end of the tax year.

question: If my salary income is Rs. 500,000 or more, how must I file my return?
reference_answer: Electronically in the prescribed form, with proof of tax deducted or paid and the wealth statement (and foreign income and assets statement if applicable).

question: How can I get more time to file my income tax return?
reference_answer: Apply in writing to the Commissioner for an extension, by the due date for filing the return.

question: When is a filed return treated as an assessment order?
reference_answer: When a complete return is furnished, the Commissioner is taken to have made an assessment and the return is treated as an assessment order.

question: How long does the Commissioner have to amend an assessment?
reference_answer: No amendment after five years from the end of the financial year in which the assessment order was issued or treated as issued.

question: What is the deadline to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against an order of the Commissioner (Appeals)?
reference_answer: Within thirty days of receiving the order.

question: Can a State-Owned Enterprise appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals) under section 127?
reference_answer: No. Section 127(1) allows any person other than a State-Owned Enterprise to appeal the listed orders.

question: When is income tax on my taxable income due for payment?
reference_answer: On the due date for furnishing the return of income for that year.

question: If the Commissioner serves a demand notice after an assessment, how long do I have to pay?
reference_answer: Within thirty days of service of the notice.

question: Is income subject to salary withholding under section 149 included when computing quarterly advance tax under section 147?
reference_answer: No. Income subject to deduction at source under section 149 is excluded from the income on which section 147 advance tax is computed.

question: How does an employer calculate the tax to deduct from my monthly salary?
reference_answer: At the employee's average rate, computed on estimated salary income for the year at Division I, Part I, First Schedule rates (including section 4AB surcharge where applicable), after adjusting tax withheld under other heads and admissible tax credits.

question: Is tax deducted from pension paid to a retired employee?
reference_answer: Under section 149(1A), where pension to a former employee below 70 exceeds Rs. 10 million in a tax year, tax is deducted on the amount above Rs. 10 million at Division I rates, along with section 4AB tax.

question: How is withholding tax on dividends deducted?
reference_answer: The payer deducts tax from the gross dividend (or collects it on dividend in specie) at the rate in Division I of Part III of the First Schedule.

question: What is the general withholding rate on dividends, for example from a REIT?
reference_answer: 15%, for Real Estate Investment Trusts and cases other than those specifically listed (Division I, Part III, First Schedule, clause (b)).

question: Who must deduct withholding tax on profit on debt under section 151?
reference_answer: Payers of yield on National Savings or Post Office accounts; banking companies and financial institutions on accounts or deposits; governments paying profit on securities; and other specified payers.

question: How is tax withheld on royalty or fees for technical services paid to a non-resident?
reference_answer: The payer deducts tax from the gross amount at the rate in Division IV of Part I of the First Schedule.

question: Do I have to withhold tax when paying a supplier for goods worth less than Rs. 75,000 in total for the year?
reference_answer: No. Section 153(1)(a) does not apply where payments for goods are less than Rs. 75,000 in aggregate in a financial year.

question: Below what yearly total do payments for services escape withholding under section 153?
reference_answer: Payments for services below Rs. 30,000 in aggregate during a financial year.

question: How much tax is deducted on export proceeds of IT services for an exporter registered with PSEB?
reference_answer: The authorized dealer deducts 0.25% of the proceeds (for tax years 2024 to 2029) when the exporter is registered with the Pakistan Software Export Board.

question: What rate is deducted on export of services proceeds if the exporter is not registered with PSEB?
reference_answer: 1% of the proceeds ('any other case', Division IVA, Part III, First Schedule).

question: An individual landlord receives Rs. 500,000 rent a year. How much tax should the tenant withhold under section 155?
reference_answer: 5% of the amount exceeding Rs. 300,000: 5% x 200,000 = Rs. 10,000 (Division V, Part III, First Schedule, slab Rs. 300,001 to 600,000).

question: What is the withholding rate on rent paid to a company?
reference_answer: 15% of the gross amount of rent (Division V, Part III, clause (b)).

question: How much tax is deducted on prize bond winnings, and is it final?
reference_answer: 15% of the gross amount paid (Division VI, Part III), and under section 156(3) the tax is a final tax.

question: What is the tax rate on lottery, raffle or quiz winnings?
reference_answer: 20% of the gross amount paid.

question: How can I stop tax being withheld from payments that are exempt or taxed at a lower rate?
reference_answer: Apply in writing (in the prescribed form) to the Commissioner for an exemption or lower rate certificate.

question: What happens if a withholding agent fails to deduct tax?
reference_answer: The person becomes personally liable to pay the tax to the Commissioner, who may pass an order and recover it after giving an opportunity of being heard.

question: How often must a withholding agent file withholding statements?
reference_answer: Quarterly, in the prescribed form.

question: Can I adjust tax deducted at source against my final tax liability?
reference_answer: Yes, subject to exceptions: tax collected or deducted is treated as tax paid, and a tax credit is allowed for the tax year in which it was collected or deducted.

question: What does it mean when tax deducted is a 'final tax' under section 169?
reference_answer: The income is not chargeable under any head in computing taxable income, and no deduction is allowed for expenditure incurred in deriving it.

question: How long does the Commissioner have to decide my refund application?
reference_answer: Within sixty days of receiving the application, the Commissioner must serve a written order after giving an opportunity of being heard.

question: Do I get compensation if my tax refund is delayed?
reference_answer: Yes. If the refund is not paid within three months of becoming due, compensation is paid at KIBOR plus 0.5% per annum for the delay.

question: For how many years must a taxpayer keep accounts and records?
reference_answer: Six years after the end of the tax year they relate to, or until pending proceedings are finally decided.

question: Can an online marketplace let unregistered vendors sell on its platform?
reference_answer: No. Under section 181(1A) online marketplaces or courier services in e-commerce must not let a vendor use their platform unless the vendor is registered under the Ordinance.

question: Under which provision does FBR maintain the Active Taxpayers' List?
reference_answer: Section 181A empowers the Board to institute the active taxpayers' list, regulated as prescribed.

question: If an individual files the return after the due date, are they included in the Active Taxpayers' List?
reference_answer: Not for that year, unless they pay a surcharge on late filing: Rs. 25,000 for an individual (Rs. 50,000 for an AOP, Rs. 100,000 for a company).

question: Do I need an NTN to get a commercial electricity or gas connection?
reference_answer: Yes. An application for a commercial or industrial electricity or gas connection is not processed unless the applicant is registered under section 181.

question: What rate of default surcharge applies to tax paid late?
reference_answer: Twelve percent or KIBOR plus three percent per annum, whichever is higher, on the unpaid amount (advance tax under section 147 is excluded).

question: Who can apply for an advance ruling under the Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: A non-resident taxpayer, by written application to the Board, about a proposed or completed transaction.

question: How much advance tax does a bank deduct on cash withdrawals by a person not on the Active Taxpayers' List?
reference_answer: 0.8% of cash withdrawals exceeding Rs. 50,000 in aggregate in a single day.

question: Is advance income tax collected on a domestic electricity bill if the consumer is on the Active Taxpayers' List?
reference_answer: No. The proviso to section 235(1) excludes a domestic consumer whose name appears on the Active Taxpayers' List.

question: Is advance income tax collected on internet bills and prepaid internet cards?
reference_answer: Yes, section 236 collects advance tax on telephone and internet bills and prepaid cards at Division V, Part IV rates.

question: How much advance tax does the seller pay when an immovable property is transferred?
reference_answer: The registering authority collects from the seller 2.75% of the gross consideration received.

question: How much advance tax does a buyer pay when purchasing immovable property?
reference_answer: 1.25% of the fair market value, collected from the purchaser by the registering authority.

question: Is tax deducted when I pay a foreign merchant with my debit or credit card?
reference_answer: Yes. The bank collects adjustable advance tax at 0.5% of the gross amount remitted abroad.

question: What capital gains tax rate applies to immovable property sold within one year of acquisition?
reference_answer: 15% where the holding period does not exceed one year (Division VIII, Part I; for property acquired on or after 1 July 2024 the 15% applies to persons on the Active Taxpayers' List).

question: What capital gains tax applies to listed shares acquired after 1 July 2024 and sold by a person on the Active Taxpayers' List?
reference_answer: 15% for persons on the Active Taxpayers' List on the acquisition and disposal dates; for others, the Division I (individuals/AOPs) or Division II (companies) rates apply.

question: For tax year 2027, how much tax does a salaried individual (salary over 75% of taxable income) pay on taxable income of Rs. 1,000,000?
reference_answer: 1% of the amount exceeding Rs. 600,000: 1% x 400,000 = Rs. 4,000 (Division I, Part I, First Schedule, salaried table, serial 2).

question: What is the top slab of income tax for non-salaried individuals and AOPs?
reference_answer: Taxable income above Rs. 5,600,000: Rs. 1,610,000 plus 45% of the amount above Rs. 5,600,000; the 45% is 40% for an AOP that is a professional firm prohibited from incorporating.
